newsitem.title: USA: Stocks rally for third day on mild inflation news.
newsitem.headline: Stocks rally for third day on mild inflation news.

text.p: Stocks rallied for a third day Friday as bonds rose sharply on news that inflation was under control.
At 1 p.m. EST, the Dow Jones industrial average was up 44.26 points at 6.868.12. In the broader market, advances led declines by 13 to nine on volume of about 313 million shares.

Bonds rallied after the government said inflation was much lower than expected in the fourth quarter, even though the nation's gross domestic product grew at a surprisingly robust 4.7 percent annual rate.
The implicit price deflator, a broad measure of inflation, rose 1.4 percent, considerably less than forecast, after a 1.7 percent gain in the third quarter.
The benchmark 30-year Treasury bond jumped nearly a full point, reducing its yield to 6.79 percent from 6.87 percent at Thursday's close. The yield and the price move in opposite directions.

"It looks like we are back on track," said Hildergard Zagorski, analyst at Prudential Securities. "This was the smallest increase in the deflator since the first quarter of 1967. "The report show the economy growing strongly and inflation low. It's the best of all possible worlds."
The Nasdaq Composite index was up 10.24 points at 1,381.26.
"We're seeing the tail end of seasonal flows into the market. A lot of index money is coming in, but it remains a narrow advance," said Michael Metz, chief investment strategist at Oppenheimer & Co.
A second economic release, the Chicago Purchasing Managers Index, bolstered the market's optimism. The index came in at 55.9 for January, below the 57.4 forecast and December's revised 57.1 reading.
"It was a confirmation of the non-inflationary prices number in the GDP," said Phil Orlando, chief investment officer of Value Line's Asset Management division.

High technology stocks were in the forefront again as Intel Corp., up 2-3/4 at 162-7/8, resumed its rally from Thursday. Netscape Communications Corp. rose 2-1/2 to 38-1/8 after Cowen & Co. initiated coverage of the stock with a buy recommendation.

"Techs, financials and energy stocks are strong, and these are the three groups we suggest investors continue to ride because that is where the earnings are coming from," Orlando said. "In a slow growth environment, these companies are producing 10 percent to 15 percent earnings growth."
Among banks, Citicorp was up 1 at 115-1/8 and and Chase Manhattan Corp. up 7/8 at 92-5/8.

Among special situations, shares of Rational Software Corp. were down 4-1/4 at 23 on speculation that its latest product will be delayed. Shares of SQA Inc., which agreed in November to merge with Rational, fell in tandem, 4-1/8 to 19-1/4.
Topping the NYSE most active list was Trigon Health Inc., up 3-1/4 at 16-1/4 on its first day of trading.
Learning Co. Inc. fell 3-1/4 to 12-3/4 after Oppenheimer & Co. lowered its rating on the stock to market performer from outperformer, market sources said.
